$comment: Response to filesystem.download (ADR 0028). Sent ONLY on success - every refusal is an error frame, unlike filesystem.content which carries its denials in-band with success:false. That difference is forced by the destination: a preview denial has a pane to render itself into, a download denial does not, because the HTTP body on that path is the file. There is no `mime` field, and its absence is a decision: Central answers every download as application/octet-stream with nosniff, so the platform never hands the browser a content type that would make it render node content inside the console's own origin.

path.$comment: Workspace-relative, and it is the path the daemon actually resolved - which is why it is echoed rather than assumed by the caller.

size.$comment: Bytes before base64. minimum 0 because an empty file is downloadable, the same reason filesystem-stored.size allows 0. The maximum is the download ceiling, which equals the upload ceiling so one number bounds both directions.

data.$comment: Canonical standard-alphabet base64, capped at the base64 length of 4 MiB. minLength 0 accepts the empty file. Base64 rather than a binary frame because the binary kinds (1 = input, 2 = output) belong to the terminal and adding a third would put file bytes on the path that carries keystrokes.
